title: Bram and the Wardrobe
premise: Zephyrine Voss, once the conservatory's most celebrated pianist, returns years after a public breakdown to work as its janitor, invisible among the students she once outshone. There she meets Anselm Brau, the last fluent speaker of a dying Alpine language, who asks her to become his final student — not of words alone, but of a family history encoded in them. As Zephyrine learns the language, she is drawn into the Brau family's long-buried question: what did their mother choose to forget, and what did the rest of them arrange their lives around to protect that forgetting? The novel ends with Zephyrine performing the language's last song at Anselm's deathbed, choosing truth over the family's comfortable silence, and finding in the fractured Braus — and in her own return to the piano — a family chosen rather than inherited.
about_author: Ivo Pemberton is the pen name of a former conservatory custodian who spent a decade sweeping concert halls before publishing essays on music and memory. This is their second novel.

chapters.title: The Tenant
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She mops the conservatory's practice halls at dawn, unrecognized by students who study posters of her younger self. Establishes her self-exile: she lives like a tenant in her own life. Emotional beat: quiet shame disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Anselm Brau
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. An elderly man asks her, of all people, for help carrying recordings to the archive room; he hears her hum a phrase no one has played in decades. He introduces himself as the last speaker of Vessik, a mountain language. Beat: first crack in her sealed life.

chapters.title: One Final Student
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. He formally asks Zephyrine to be his last student, admitting he chose her because prodigies understand loss. She refuses; he leaves her a tape anyway. Beat: the offer that cannot be unheard.

chapters.title: What the Tape Says
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Alone at night she plays the tape: a lullaby in Vessik, then a woman's voice — Anselm's mother — mid-sentence, cut off. Zephyrine realizes the recording was deliberately broken. Beat: curiosity overriding grief.

chapters.title: Lessons
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. First lessons in the conservatory's boiler room: sounds, kinship words, the grammar of obligation. Anselm teaches slowly, testing whether she can bear what the language carries. Beat: tentative trust between two exiles.

chapters.title: The Family Arrangement
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She meets Anselm's siblings at his Sunday dinner: Marta, who runs the household like a fortress; Tomas, the cheerful one who changes the subject; Ilse, silent, watchful. Everyone orbits around the absent mother, now in a care home with advancing dementia. Beat: warmth with a locked room inside it.

chapters.title: Kinship Words
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. Vessik has no word for 'stranger' but twelve for kinds of belonging. He reflects on why he never taught his own children. Flashback to 1974: the mother speaking Vessik to him by the lake, then stopping forever. Beat: tenderness shadowed by guilt.

chapters.title: The Question
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Marta confronts Zephyrine: whatever Father is teaching you, leave it buried. Zephyrine realizes the whole family arranged itself around a single unasked question about the mother. Beat: loyalty demanded before truth is even spoken.

chapters.title: Practice Room
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A student recognizes her playing scales on the basement piano and wordlessly leaves the room. Old colleague Doro offers her a recital slot; she declines, but plays afterward, alone, until her hands shake. Beat: the return of want.

chapters.title: Ilse
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The silent sister takes Zephyrine walking and shows her the lake from the tapes. In fragments she reveals she was there the summer the mother stopped speaking Vessik — and that she remembers everything. Beat: an ally found in the family's quietest member.

chapters.title: The Care Home
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Visiting the mother, Zephyrine speaks a Vessik greeting; the old woman's eyes clear for ten seconds and she answers in full sentences, calling Zephyrine by another name — 'Lene.' Beat: the past reaching through dementia.

chapters.title: Who Was Lene
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. Shaken, Anselm admits Lene was his sister, dead at nineteen, the true prodigy, whose death the mother blamed herself for — and whose story the family rewrote. He stops the lessons. Beat: betrayal shaped like protection.

chapters.title: Marta's Version
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta tells Zephyrine her version: the mother chose forgetting to survive, and love means honoring that choice. She offers Zephyrine a place in the family if she lets it lie. Beat: the seduction of loyal silence.

chapters.title: The Broken Tape
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Splicing the damaged recording, Zephyrine hears the mother's full account of Lene's drowning — and the father's role in it, which the siblings never knew. Beat: knowledge as burden; she must decide what truth owes whom.

chapters.title: Duty
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas, the peacemaker, privately begs Zephyrine to stay away: the mother is fading, and the family's fragile peace is all they have left. His own marriage collapsed under the weight of pretending. Beat: sympathy for the lie.

chapters.title: Recital
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine finally accepts Doro's recital slot, playing publicly for the first time since her breakdown. Halfway through she falters — then keeps going, imperfectly. The Brau siblings attend without being asked. Beat: reclaiming authorship of her own story.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Lake
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. At the lakeside house, Zephyrine plays the restored tape to the gathered family. Marta denies it, Tomas breaks down, Ilse confirms it, Anselm says nothing. The arrangement shatters. Beat: climax — truth detonating the found family's foundation.

chapters.title: What Forgetting Cost
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. Anselm walks the frozen shore all night and admits he taught Zephyrine hoping someone would ask the question he couldn't. He visits the mother, who mistakes him for his dead father, and forgives her aloud. Beat: grief transmuted into release.

chapters.title: The Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Hospital now. Anselm, failing, teaches her the final song — the one sung when a speaker dies, so the language knows how to say goodbye. She learns it perfectly, knowing perfection is the least of it. Beat: devotion beyond duty.

chapters.title: Vessik
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Anselm dies holding her hand as she sings the last song in Vessik. The siblings stand together in the doorway — estranged from the old arrangement, bound to each other still. Beat: elegy; a language ends, a family begins.

chapters.title: Owners
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Spring. Zephyrine records what she knows of Vessik for the archive, tutors Ilse's granddaughter in the first words, and signs a lease — her own name, her own flat. No longer a tenant. Beat: quiet resolution.

chapters.title: Coda: Twelve Kinds of Belonging
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. At a small gathering in the boiler room-turned-music room, the surviving Braus and Zephyrine share dinner; the mother, near the end, smiles at a Vessik lullaby without fear. Zephyrine plays. Beat: found family, truth intact, love chosen over duty.
